front: How do you build the matrix of a transformation from the unit square?
back: First column = image of $(1, 0)$; second column = image of $(0, 1)$.

front: Matrices for reflection in the $x$-axis and in the $y$-axis
Matrices for reflection in $y = x$ and in $y = -x$
Matrices for rotations about the origin
Matrix for an enlargement, centre $O$, scale factor $k$
Matrices for a stretch and a shear with the $x$-axis invariant (factor $k$)
notes: With the $y$-axis invariant: stretch $\begin{pmatrix} k & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$, shear $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ k & 1 \end{pmatrix}$.

back: $QP$: the transformation done first goes on the right.

front: Matrix of the inverse transformation of $M$
back: $M^{-1}$: it maps every image back onto its object.
notes: A singular matrix (determinant 0) has no inverse.

front: What does the determinant of a transformation matrix tell you about area?
back: Area of image $= |\det M| \times$ area of object.
notes: A negative determinant means the orientation is reversed.

front: Which point is invariant under every $2 \times 2$ matrix transformation?
back: The origin, so translations cannot be written as $2 \times 2$ matrices.
